questions.lead: A flight from Ft. Lauderdale to Tampa (197 miles), leaving on 17 February 2001 in the afternoon.
questions.ask: The flight arrives at least three hours late.
questions.claim: A flight from Ft. Lauderdale to Tampa (197 miles), leaving on 17 February 2001 in the afternoon. The flight arrives at least three hours late.
questions.fact: This flight arrived 18 minutes late. Of the other 78 flights that left Ft. Lauderdale in the afternoon in this January to March 2001 sample, 3% arrived at least three hours late.
questions.why: A long delay is the exception for any one flight, so the base rate for the airport and time of day is the anchor. Rare does not mean never: on the 1% dial the difference between 2% and 8% is worth real points, so say the figure the records give, not a round number.
questions.src_name: US Bureau of Transportation Statistics on-time data, January to March 2001 (a 20,000-flight sample), via vega-datasets
